title: Python Language Fundamentals
relevance: Campus and early SDE interviews and OAs routinely probe core Python semantics—typing, identity vs equality, data types, and floating-point behavior—to screen for language fluency before harder coding problems.

phases.goal: Establish what Python is and the core language properties candidates must name accurately.

must_hit.point: Python is a high-level, interpreted, general-purpose language that supports objects, modules, threads, exception-handling, and automatic memory management.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate calls it high-level and interpreted/general-purpose and names at least some of objects, modules, threads, exceptions, or automatic memory management.

must_hit.point: Python is dynamically typed: type-checking happens during execution because it runs statements line by line; it is also strongly typed, so "1" + 2 raises a type error rather than coercing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts static vs dynamic checking and says Python checks types at runtime; may note strong typing vs JavaScript-style weak coercion.

must_hit.point: PEP stands for Python Enhancement Proposal; PEP 8 documents Python code style guidelines expected for open-source contribution.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate expands PEP and ties PEP 8 specifically to style guidelines, not language features.

must_hit.point: Built-in types group into NoneType, Numeric (int, float, complex; bool is a sub-type of integers), Sequence (list, tuple, range), Mapping (dict), Set (set, frozenset), and Callable types; type() and isinstance() check types.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists several categories correctly and notes dict as the standard mapping and set vs frozenset.

must_hit.point: The Zen of Python is a collection of 19 guiding principles for writing programs that influence Python’s design (e.g., readability counts; explicit is better than implicit).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says ~19 principles and can quote or paraphrase at least one Zen line.

probes: What is Python, and what are the main benefits of using it?
What does it mean that Python is a dynamically typed language?
What is PEP 8 and why does it matter?

hints.1: Think about how Python runs code and when types are checked.
hints.2: Separate language kind (interpreted, general-purpose), typing model (dynamic + strong), and community style (PEP 8 / Zen).
hints.3: Python executes line by line with runtime type checks; "1" + 2 errors; PEP 8 is the style PEP; Zen has 19 guiding principles.

phases.goal: Verify concrete mechanics of operators, identity, strings, floats, and documentation.

must_hit.point: Ternary form is [on true] if [expression] else [on false] (no C++-style ?:); e.g. with a, b = 2, 3, min = a if a < b else b prints 2.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate writes or verbally gives the if-else expression form and the min example outcome.

must_hit.point: `is` / `is not` compare identity (same memory location); `==` / `!=` compare values; equal values need not be identical.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate clearly separates memory identity from value equality.

must_hit.point: Python caches small integers in the range -5 to 256, so a = 256 and b = 256 can make a is b True, while a = 257 and b = 257 can make a is b False even though a == b is True.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate cites the -5..256 cache and the 257 counterexample for is vs ==.

must_hit.point: Operator precedence descends from () through **, unary +x/-x/~x, */ // %, +-, shifts, &, ^, |, comparisons/identity/membership, then not, and, or.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate places parentheses and ** high and logical or lowest, or walks the major bands correctly.

must_hit.point: Strings are arrays of bytes representing Unicode characters; there is no separate character type (a single character is a string of length 1); strings are immutable.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says Unicode/immutable and no char type—length-1 string.

must_hit.point: 0.3 - 0.2 is not equal to 0.1 because floats are stored in binary (base-2) and values like 0.1 cannot be represented exactly, causing floating-point inaccuracy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate blames binary floating-point precision, not a Python bug.

must_hit.point: Docstrings are string literals right after a function, method, class, or module definition and are accessed via the object’s __doc__ attribute.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate places the docstring immediately after the definition and names __doc__.

probes: What does the is operator do, and how does it differ from ==?
Explain the ternary operator in Python.
Why is 0.3 - 0.2 not equal to 0.1 in Python?

hints.1: Focus on memory location vs value, and on how floats are stored.
hints.2: Cover ternary syntax, is vs == with the integer cache, string immutability, and binary float precision.
hints.3: is checks identity; small ints -5..256 are cached; 257 may not share identity; ternary is x if cond else y; 0.1 isn’t exact in binary float; docstrings live in __doc__.

phases.goal: Surface known Python limitations and when related constructs differ in intent.

must_hit.point: As an interpreted high-level language, Python is slower than C/C++ or Java because execution goes through an interpreter rather than a compiler.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate links speed cost to interpretation vs compiled languages.

must_hit.point: Dynamic typing means many errors appear only at runtime, so more testing is required.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate connects dynamic typing to deferred/runtime errors and testing burden.

must_hit.point: Python is weak for mobile development and has high memory use for memory-intensive work due to flexible data types; its DB access layer is described as underdeveloped vs JDBC/ODBC.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names at least two of: mobile weakness, high memory, primitive DB access.

must_hit.point: set is mutable (add/remove); frozenset is immutable and cannot be modified after creation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts mutability of set vs frozenset.

probes: What are the main disadvantages of Python?
When would you choose a frozenset over a set?

hints.1: Think about speed, memory, mobile, and when type errors show up.
hints.2: Separate runtime/performance costs from mutability choices on set types.
hints.3: Slower than C/C++/Java via interpreter; runtime type errors need more tests; weak on mobile/high memory; set mutable, frozenset not.

phases.goal: Apply fundamentals to packaging vocabulary and choosing is vs == correctly in real answers.

must_hit.point: A module is a Python file meant to be imported; a package is a folder of related modules often with __init__.py; a library is a loose umbrella for a bundle of code (the Standard Library has hundreds of modules).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate maps module→file, package→folder (+ __init__.py), library→bundle/standard library.

must_hit.point: Use == when comparing values and is when you need identity (same object in memory)—do not assume equal integers share identity outside the small-int cache.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate gives a practical rule: == for values, is for identity/singletons-style checks, wary of 257-style pitfalls.

must_hit.point: Mappings map hashable values to objects, are mutable, and the standard mapping type is the dictionary; sequence types support in / not in for membership.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate mentions dict as the mapping type and membership operators on sequences.

probes: How do modules, packages, and libraries differ in Python?
Identity operator (is) vs equality operator (==)—when do you use each?
What are Python docstrings and how do you read them?

hints.1: Start from file vs folder vs “bundle of code.”
hints.2: Define module/package/library, then say when is is safe vs when == is required.
hints.3: Module=importable file; package=related modules in a folder with __init__.py; library=umbrella/Standard Library; == for values, is for identity; docstrings via __doc__.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: is/is not compare whether two names refer to the same object in memory; ==/!= compare values. Equal values are not necessarily identical—e.g. a = 257; b = 257 can yield a is b False while a == b True; small integers from -5 to 256 may be cached so a is b can be True.

A module is one importable Python file (classes/functions/variables). A package is a collection of related modules in a folder, often with __init__.py. A library is a loose umbrella for a bundle of code; the Python Standard Library ships hundreds of modules.
set is mutable and supports add() and remove(); frozenset is immutable and cannot be changed after creation.

Python’s interpreter-based execution is slower than compiled C/C++ or Java; it is strong on desktop/server but weak for mobile; flexible types raise memory use; dynamic typing pushes more errors to runtime and needs more testing; DB access is called primitive vs JDBC/ODBC.

gotchas.trap: Assuming a is b whenever a == b for integers.
gotchas.correction: is checks identity, not value. Small ints -5..256 may be cached (256 is 256 can be True); 257 and 257 may be False for is while == is True.
Python uses [on true] if [expression] else [on false], e.g. a if a < b else b.
Floats use binary base-2 representation; values like 0.1 are not exact, so floating-point results can disagree with decimal intuition.

gotchas.trap: Treating a single character as a distinct char type.
gotchas.correction: Python has no character type; a single character is a string of length 1, and strings are immutable Unicode.

gotchas.trap: Confusing strong vs weak typing with static vs dynamic checking.
gotchas.correction: Strong typing (Python) rejects "1" + 2; weak typing (e.g. JavaScript) may coerce to "12". Static checking is before execution; dynamic checking (Python) is during execution.

gotchas.trap: Calling any folder of code a module or any import a package.
gotchas.correction: Module = importable file; package = collection of modules in a folder (often with __init__.py); library = broad bundle term.
